title: Jamia Moves All Classes Online as Students' Union Protest Enters Day 13
excerpt: Jamia Millia Islamia cited student safety for the shift, in force until further notice. Hunger strikers are demanding restoration of the students' union, dissolved in 2006, and the Chief Proctor's removal.
body:
• Jamia Millia Islamia in New Delhi shifted all classes online with immediate effect on October 24, until further notice, as a precautionary measure for student safety.
  • Students have protested since October 12 — day 13 on Saturday — demanding restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU), dissolved in 2006; several are on hunger strike.
  • Protesters also want the Chief Proctor removed over an alleged crackdown; the All India Students' Association alleged hunger strikers were attacked on Saturday, a claim the university had not publicly answered in the reports.
  • Students should follow the online schedule and official university channels — no date has been given for in-person classes to resume, and the October 29-November 1 Foundation Day event has already been cancelled.

Jamia Millia Islamia moved every class at the university online on Saturday, October 24, as a student protest demanding restoration of the students' union entered its 13th day. The shift is effective immediately and stays in force until further notice.

"The Competent Authority, JMI, has decided to conduct classes of all courses of the University through online mode with immediate effect until further notice."

— Jamia Millia Islamia, official statement

The university said the decision was taken to ensure the safety and security of bona fide students on campus, to safeguard their academic interests and to keep teaching going without undue disruption. A notice from the Office of the Registrar, dated October 24, directed deans, heads, directors and faculty to follow the online schedule, run classes on online platforms and supply students with academic support and learning materials. Any change will be announced through official university channels.

What the protesters want

The protest began on October 12. Its central demand is the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union, the university's elected student body, which was dissolved in 2006; Jamia has held no student union elections since, a grievance students have carried for two decades. Several students are on hunger strike, and protesters are also demanding the removal of the university's Chief Proctor over what they describe as a crackdown on demonstrators.

https://x.com/RanaAyyub/status/2113959701386076289

Clashes and competing claims

Reports from the campus describe friction between protesting students and university security guards, and a row over graffiti found on campus walls, including 'Free Kashmir' and 'Free Palestine' slogans. Student representatives have distanced the movement from the graffiti; one protest voice, Anas, was reported as urging the administration to check security camera footage to identify who was responsible. The All India Students' Association (AISA) alleged on Saturday that the administration had begun assaulting hunger strikers and dismantling the protest site during negotiations, calling it, in its words, the most brutal face of the Jamia administration. The university had not publicly responded to that specific allegation in the reports published on Saturday; its stated position remains the safety rationale in its notice.

The disruption is already widening beyond the classroom. The university has cancelled its 106th Foundation Day celebrations, the 'Talimi Mela' scheduled on campus from October 29 to November 1, citing the continuing protest.

What happens next

There is no timeline for a return to in-person teaching. The immediate questions are whether the university concedes a process on the union — a drafting committee on JMISU has featured in earlier appeals to end the agitation — and whether the hunger strike escalates. For students, the practical position is simple: classes continue online, attendance follows the online schedule, and the next announcement, whenever it comes, will come through the university's official channels.
